notes: Context: Kestrel runs real-time reranking + personalization for programmatic ad auctions. Tight latency needs, extremely high short-lived QPS.
Primary ask: formal throughput guarantee for Dedicated pool (min tokens/sec) + explicit concurrency caps and burst policy with predictable billing.

Targets from customer: sustain 250k-300k tokens/sec for steady-state across the reserved pool, support bursts to ~1.0-1.2M tokens/sec for 20-40s, p50 latency <= 60ms on <=128-token requests, 99.9% availability on dedicated lanes.

GPU planning: customer prefers H100-class performance; current POC on 4x H100-equivalent. Expecting recommendation for 8x H100-equivalent to meet steady + burst SLAs with headroom for autoscaling/burst pools.
Concurrency: asking for guidance on request concurrency caps (suggested 4k short concurrent requests) and graceful throttling/fallback behavior when limits reached.

Billing/penalties: Kestrel wants credits if min tokens/sec falls below guarantee for longer than 5 minutes; questions on how burst is met — pre-provisioned burst lanes vs. elastic cloud burst at different price tiers.

Quote from CTO: "We need deterministic serving economics during campaigns — spikes without surprise bills. If you can give a guaranteed tokens/sec floor + a clean burst policy, we can sign a 12-month reserved contract."

Security: must support SSO (SAML), KMS for key control, audit logs exported to their SIEM, and data residency for EU customers in future. Proposal should include SOC2 timeline and encryption-in-transit + at-rest checklist.

POC notes: observed degradation when KV cache warmed cold on multi-tenant fallback; SE recommends prefix caching + sticky routing for ad-serving keys to reduce tail latency. Jordan to provide config knobs.

Negotiation points open: min tokens/sec metric definition (aggregate vs per-shard), measurement windows, burst charging methodology (flat retainer vs usage-based overage), and concurrency vs latency SLO tradeoffs.
sla_negotiation_points: Define min_tokens_per_sec: measured as 5-min rolling aggregate across reserved pool or 1-min? Customer prefers 1-min for campaign spikes; Redwood prefers 5-min to avoid microbursts counting as failure.
Burst policy: pre-provisioned burst capacity (charged at reserved rate) OR elastic cloud burst (pay-as-you-go higher rate). Kestrel requests capped elastic bursts with predictable top-up pricing.
Concurrency caps: set soft cap at 4k concurrent short requests with 95th-percentile throttling; need deterministic fallback (serve lighter model or queue) — discuss automatic model fallbacks.
Penalties/credits: service credits for sustained < min_tokens_per_sec beyond 5 consecutive minutes; formula TBD (daily pro-rated credit up to 20% of monthly bill).
Incident response SLA: 1h P1 response, 24h root-cause for major availability incidents; request dedicated escalation path during campaign windows.
poc_results_summary: Baseline (4x H100-eq): 290k sustained tokens/sec (128-token requests) during replay; p50 latency 52ms, p95 210ms under sustained load.
Cold KV cache increases p95 to ~480ms for a 10% sample of requests — mitigation: prefix caching and sticky routing; potential config reduces p95 to ~160ms.
Burst test (elastic burst): reached 850k tokens/sec for 25s before throttling; customer wants repeatable 1.0M+ bursts without throttling.
Estimate to meet SLOs: 8x H100-eq reserved + small elastic buffer (20%) for short bursts; optimize suggests batching reduction and prefix cache to reduce required GPUs by ~15%.
commercial_notes: Customer open to 12-month reserved commit if throughput guarantee and burst billing are acceptable.

Finance asks for unit pricing per reserved H100-eq lane and explicit overage rate for burst consumption; proposing two options: (A) pre-purchased burst credits at discounted rate, (B) pay-as-you-go burst at 2.5x reserved unit price.
Estimated ARR range provided by customer aligns with $500k-$1M given expected traffic volume and 12-month term.
